key_insight: A two-stage quantum-classical workflow uses quantum sampling over guaranteed-feasible spanning trees to speed up distribution network reconfiguration.
engineering_relevance: The approach targets lower-loss power distribution operation by reducing the search burden on a MISOCP solver while respecting electrical and topological constraints.
method: Build a cycle-edge encoding that represents only spanning trees and can be scaled to fit the available qubit budget.
Run iterative linear-ramp QAOA to sample feasible topologies from these subspaces.
Use the quantum-derived sample distribution to warm-start a mixed-integer second-order-cone programming solver.
evidence_signal: The method was tested on six distribution networks from 33 to 417 buses in simulation and on trapped-ion hardware, where the guided MISOCP reached within 1% of the best-known solution in less median time than the unguided solver.
watch_item: Performance depends on how well the sampled subspace and hardware output capture high-quality topologies, so limited qubit budgets or noisy sampling may reduce gains.
paper_title: Two-Stage Quantum-Classical Distribution Network Reconfiguration via Cycle-Edge Encoding
